title: Google Paid Apple $1 Billion to be Default Search on iPhone, iPad
main_content:
Search giant Google reportedly paid archnemesis Apple $1 billion to remain the default search engine for Apple’s mobile devices, according to a report by Bloomberg News.

Bloomberg made the claim based on court documents in a copyright lawsuit filed by Oracle Corporation against Google.

Google, which is now under the umbrella company Alphabet, pays Apple a percentage of the revenue it earns via search, but the exact percentage has never been disclosed.

Bloomberg reported the revenue sharing reached as high as 34 percent.

The court paper cited by the news agency is no longer available online, and neither Apple nor Google have commented.

Bloomberg reported that the transcript vanished without a trace from electronic court records earlier this week.

Oracle’s lawsuit claimed Google used its Java software to develop Android, Google’s mobile operating system, but never paid for it.

According to the BBC, the $1 billion amount has been reported before by firms such as Morgan Stanley.

“It’s a very lucrative business to be the browser of choice on a device or the search engine on a device,” Chris Green, a technology analyst at Lewis, told the BBC.

Alphabet launched in August of 2015 and is run by Google’s current leaders, including CEO Larry Page and his team of co-founder Sergey Brin and CFO Ruth Porat.

questions.question: Why has Google paid Apple $1 billion so far?
options: To terminate a lawsuit filed by Oracle Corporation
To retain the status of default search engine on Apple devices
To increase its revenue share from Apple
To fund Apple's development of new mobile features
questions.answer: To retain the status of default search engine on Apple devices

questions.question: According to the article, what does Google pay Apple?
options: A fixed annual payment of $1 billion
An undisclosed percentage of search revenue
A flat fee for each Apple device sold
A one-time licensing payment for Safari
questions.answer: An undisclosed percentage of search revenue

questions.question: Why did Oracle sue Google?
options: For using Java software without compensation
For unfair competition in mobile advertising
For not complying with software licensing agreements
For breach of contract in search engine services
questions.answer: For using Java software without compensation
